headline: A rough day on the ASX — PLS and GXAI hit hard — but the RBA held rates steady, giving mortgage holders a breather.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a tough session today, dropping 6.3% to close at $5.04. Lithium prices remain under pressure as the market figures out where demand is heading — EVs are slowing as the main driver, and while battery storage is emerging as a new use case, it's not yet picking up the slack. PLS is now sitting at a 25% loss on your total investment.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI dropped 5% today to close at $17.53, dragged lower partly by weakness in big AI-linked US stocks like Alphabet (GOOG fell 2.2% last night). The ETF holds global AI companies, so when the US AI names sell off, this one follows. You're now down about 7.2% on your total investment here.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft had a strong session last night, jumping 5.7% to $372.97. No specific news catalyst in the data, but MSFT has been the market's favourite AI story — investors keep piling in relative to Google. This is a bright spot in your portfolio, though you're still down about 15.8% overall on this position.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE fell 2.4% today to $92.90, which is a meaningful single-day move for a broad emerging markets fund. Weakness in global risk appetite tends to hit emerging markets harder, and a soft session across Asian markets contributed to the pullback.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google slipped 2.2% to $334.69 last night. No company-specific news drove the fall — the market continues to favour Microsoft's AI narrative over Google's, and that gap showed up again in last night's session. You're still up about 8.9% overall on this small position.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS fell 1.5% today to $523.20, reflecting the mixed US session from last night — the S&P 500 and NASDAQ both dipped slightly. As a broad US market fund, VTS tracks the overall mood in America, which was a bit cautious last night.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG edged down 0.6% today to $76.54 — a pretty minor move for a diversified fund that holds a mix of Aussie and global shares. The small dip reflects the generally cautious tone on markets today. You're still slightly in the green overall on this one.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL bucked the trend today, rising 0.9% to $8.10. Interesting given that crude oil actually fell 3.7% last night — the ETF may be catching up from previous weakness or reflecting currency movements. Keep an eye on oil prices; if the slide continues, FUEL could give back today's gains.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO was basically flat last night, down just 0.08% to $238.53. GTA VI is confirmed as a digital-only launch with pre-orders tied to the GTA+ subscription — a smart move for recurring revenue. The stock is holding steady ahead of what could be a massive launch catalyst.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Lithium rout deepens
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals dropped another 6.3% today to $5.04, and you're now down 25% on this position overall. The lithium story is shifting — EV demand growth is slowing, and battery storage isn't yet filling the gap. There's no obvious near-term catalyst to reverse this. Worth asking yourself if you still believe in the long-term thesis before averaging down.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF takes a 5% hit
watch_today.detail: GXAI fell 5% today and is now down 7.2% on your total investment. The fund tracks global AI companies, so it's closely tied to how US AI stocks are performing — and last night's weakness in GOOG dragged it lower. Nothing structurally broken here, but it's worth watching whether US AI names can stabilise this week before the US market opens tonight.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Big night, but still underwater overall
watch_today.detail: Microsoft jumped 5.7% last night to $372.97 — a genuinely strong session. It's been consistently outperforming GOOG on the AI narrative. Even with this pop, you're still down ~15.8% on your total investment in MSFT. If you believe in the AI story, this is a hold — but don't be lulled into complacency by one good night.

watch_today.title: RBA holds interest rates — good news for your mortgage, mixed for markets
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank left rates on hold today. That's a relief for anyone with a mortgage and means the cash rate isn't going higher right now. For your ASX holdings, stable rates tend to be supportive — less pressure on company borrowing costs. Watch for any RBA statement commentary on future cuts, which could move markets this week.

watch_today.title: Oil falls 3.7% — watch FUEL.AX this week
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) dropped $2.69 to $69.23 last night after the International Energy Agency cut its demand forecast. FUEL.AX actually rose slightly today, but if oil keeps sliding this week, energy company earnings get squeezed and FUEL could follow. Keep an eye on it.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA VI launch details firming up
watch_today.detail: Grand Theft Auto VI is confirmed as a digital-only launch, tied to pre-orders and the GTA+ subscription service. This is actually a smart play for Take-Two — digital means higher margins and no second-hand market. The stock is flat and holding steady. The real catalyst is the launch itself; if it delivers, this could be a big mover.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a quiet positive session today, up 0.18% to 8,764. The action was really in your individual holdings though — PLS and GXAI both got smacked. Overnight in the US, the S&P 500 barely moved (-0.05%) and the NASDAQ dipped 0.24%, so no big drama there. Gold had a strong night, up 1.6% to over $4,096 USD per ounce — a sign that some investors are still hunting for safety. Oil was the main story, dropping 3.7% to $69.23 as the IEA (International Energy Agency) trimmed its demand forecasts. The Aussie dollar was steady at 69.01 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Modest gain today — broad market held up despite some ugly individual stock moves.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Essentially flat last night — the US market is treading water.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Slight dip last night, weighed down by weakness in tech names like GOOG.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil fell sharply after the IEA cut its demand outlook — watch FUEL.AX.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold surging to record-ish territory — investors buying safety.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Rock steady — no meaningful currency movement today.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is the RBA keeping interest rates on hold — a relief for borrowers. No other major Australian political stories broke today based on available data.

stories.title: RBA leaves interest rates on hold
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia left the official cash rate on hold at today's meeting — a decision that will be welcomed by anyone with a variable-rate mortgage. It means your repayments won't be going up again just yet. For the sharemarket, stable rates reduce pressure on companies that carry debt, which is a mild positive for broader ASX holdings like VDHG. No article text was available beyond the headline, so watch for the RBA's full statement which may hint at the timing of future cuts.

ai.summary: The big AI story this week is the US government putting guardrails on who can access the newest AI models — OpenAI and Anthropic are limiting access to Trump-approved customers during a cybersecurity review. Separately, AI developers are throwing serious money at US politics to influence regulation.

stories.title: OpenAI and Anthropic limit new AI models to Trump-approved customers during cybersecurity review
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has told Anthropic it can release its new 'Mythos' AI model — but only to select companies and government agencies that have been approved during an ongoing cybersecurity review. Both OpenAI and Anthropic are playing ball, limiting who can access their newest, most powerful models. In practice, this means the latest AI tools aren't freely available to everyone right now — the US government is vetting who gets them first. This matters for companies (and ETFs like GXAI) that depend on broad commercial access to cutting-edge AI.

stories.title: AI developers and donors pledge $275M for political races as regulation battles intensify
stories.why_it_matters: AI companies and their major backers have pledged $275 million toward US political campaigns as the fight over AI regulation heats up. This is the industry trying to shape the rules before governments lock them in. The more political influence AI firms buy, the more likely regulation ends up favouring incumbents like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Microsoft — which could be good for your GOOG, MSFT and GXAI holdings long-term, but also concentrates power in a few big players.

stories.title: New commentary urges patient-centered AI regulation in healthcare
stories.why_it_matters: A new commentary published in a medical journal is calling for AI regulations in healthcare to be designed around patient needs rather than just technology company interests. As AI tools increasingly get used for medical diagnosis, treatment recommendations and hospital admin, how they're regulated will determine whether they help or harm patients. This is more of a slow-burn story — but if strong AI healthcare frameworks take hold, it opens a significant new commercial market for major AI developers.

sport.summary: NRL Round 17 wrapped up today with the Raiders and Knights both winning their Sunday games. The big storyline across the round is a horror injury toll — Melbourne Storm are in crisis mode, and the Dolphins have their own post-match surgery news. In other sport, Wimbledon is underway with Madison Keys in form and some concern around Emma Raducanu. AFL threw up a controversy in Port vs Adelaide.

stories.title: Dolphins star undergoes surgery after 'game of the season' win over Warriors
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins edged out the Warriors 26-24 in what's being called the game of the season — a thriller at Suncorp. The good news ended there though, with a key Dolphins player heading straight into surgery post-match. The full details of the injury aren't in the article text, but it's a blow for a Dolphins side that needed the win. For Gold Coast locals, worth keeping an eye on the Dolphins' injury list heading into next week.

stories.title: Storm face worst injury crisis of Craig Bellamy's coaching tenure
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne Storm got thumped 30-4 by Manly on Saturday night at 4 Pines Park, and the injury news is even worse than the scoreboard. Reports say the Storm are facing the worst injury toll of Craig Bellamy's long coaching career — a remarkable statement given how many seasons he's been at the helm. With so many bodies unavailable, expect Melbourne to struggle for the next month unless the squad can hold together.

stories.title: Cowboys beat Panthers 26-12 — big State of Origin message and a legend's milestone
stories.why_it_matters: North Queensland Cowboys defeated the Panthers 26-12 at Queensland Country Bank Stadium on Saturday — a big result that doubles as a State of Origin audition for Cowboys players. The Panthers, without injured stars, look vulnerable this season. It was also a milestone match for a Cowboys legend (details in full article), adding an emotional edge to what was already a statement win.

stories.title: Controversial Bunker call, Ricky Stuart's brutal mid-game move — Raiders beat Dragons 24-16
stories.why_it_matters: Canberra Raiders beat the Dragons 24-16 at GIO Stadium today, but the game wasn't without drama — a contentious Bunker (video review) call had people fuming, and Raiders coach Ricky Stuart made a 'brutal' mid-game tactical change that drew plenty of attention. The Raiders are building some form, while the Dragons' season continues to drift.

stories.title: Madison Keys wins Eastbourne title heading into Wimbledon; Naomi Osaka injury concern
stories.why_it_matters: Madison Keys won the Eastbourne grass court title in the lead-up to Wimbledon — perfect form and momentum heading into the first Grand Slam on grass. Keys is drawing comparisons to her 2025 Australian Open run, where she went all the way. Meanwhile, Naomi Osaka picked up an injury concern at Eastbourne which has fans worried she may not be at full fitness for Wimbledon. Emma Raducanu is also facing withdrawal speculation, which would be a blow to the home crowd hopes at the All England Club.
